nodes.label: KubernetesLease
nodes.rationale: Backed by the coordination.k8s.io/v1 Lease resource — etcd-backed, strongly consistent, RBAC-controlled. Two pods calling acquire() concurrently produce exactly one winner regardless of scheduling or partitions between them. ~6 API calls per minute per lease at a 30s TTL, negligible even with many leases.

nodes.label: KubernetesLeaseOptions
nodes.rationale: In-cluster pods need only namespace and name plus the base LeaseOptionsType fields; API URL, token and CA come from the standard mount paths.

nodes.label: The three connection fields are one credential
nodes.rationale: apiServerUrl, authToken and caCert are all-or-nothing; a partial set throws OptionsError. Previously each fell back to the in-cluster mount individually, so supplying only an apiServerUrl sent the pod's own ServiceAccount token to that host. The TLS pin limited the damage but a cluster credential has no business at an address it was not issued for. apiServerUrl must be https — the client builds a node:https request regardless, so an http:// URL was never plaintext, only confusing.

nodes.label: KubernetesLease required fields enforced at construction
nodes.rationale: Not cosmetic: without owner the Lease is written with no spec.holderIdentity (the undefined key falls out of the JSON body) and a holderless lease reads as free to every pod — every acquire() returns true and the single-holder guarantee is gone with no error logged. A missing ttlMs reaches the same result via NaN expiry.

nodes.label: resourceVersion CAS
nodes.rationale: Atomicity comes from Kubernetes' optimistic concurrency: the resourceVersion from the last read is sent back so a write is a compare-and-set, and two concurrent attempts to claim a stale lease produce one winner.

nodes.label: Renewal loop
nodes.rationale: A PUT of the whole Lease object every renewalIntervalMs with a raised renewTime. There is no retry budget inside the loop: a transient 5xx/refused/timeout, a 409 CAS conflict or a 404 all fire onLost immediately.

nodes.label: Tolerance for a corrupt or hostile lease record
nodes.rationale: Both staleness fields were written by the very holder being judged, so they are never trusted unchecked: leaseDurationSeconds counts for at most 4x the challenger's own ttlMs (generous rather than a hard clamp so a rolling upgrade that raises the TTL does not let a smaller-TTL node evict a live holder); a renewTime more than one ttlMs in the future is not credible from a working clock and counts as expired, because believing it is what lets a single write block the lease forever; a missing or unparseable renewTime counts as alive, since 'somebody holds it' is the safe reading. Worst case is 4x ttlMs of unavailability instead of an indefinite block.

nodes.label: Lease RBAC requirements
nodes.rationale: get/create/update/patch/delete on coordination.k8s.io leases; without them acquire() fails with 403. Without delete, release() still works but leaves the object behind — harmless, the next acquire reuses it. In-cluster tokens rotate automatically, so hardcoded tokens expire and need manual rotation.
